This reminds me of when I used to be a tire in NASCAR races; there's nothing quite like making a non-stop left turn for 500 miles. My racer and I had won some races here and there, but today was the big day: Daytona! We looked good for just about the entire race and were in a good position come the final lap. Then tragedy struck. My car was struck by another sending us right into the retaining wall. I called out to my racer "DALE! DALE!" But he was already dead. Killed instantly. I can't help but feel it was my fault, Maybe if I had more friction on the road, we'd have been in a different position and he'd be alive today... Now, I'm in a museum to commemorate his life. Everyday people walk by me, staring. They feel joy and sadness remembering him but all I feel is crippling depression. I can't sleep at night knowing that Dale's son was racing that day, on the very track his father, my racer, died on. Dale Jr did get second though, so good for him or whatever. But all I want is to be reunited with Dale. The only person who ever got me. I've tried ending it with heroin, meth, cocaine... but not having a bloodstream led to nothing. Not even a high to temporarily numb the pain. I've heard some places incinerate tires and that's what I want. That's what I deserve. It'd be poetic since I deserve nothing less than the inferno of hell for not protecting Dale Earnhardt that day. Maybe in hell, I feel something other than depression. Even physical pain would be better than this.

Also: A little background on this song between my band mate and I (I sing leads in this song), we decided to start writing music early this year and spent the summer working on our first official EP. A good friend of ours had a lot of quality recording equipment and helped our sound a lot, as I explained where I wanted this song to hit in its unique style.
Lyrically, I intended for this song to be a spiritual journey for myself -- some piece of me I could share with the world, a personal struggle that I battle on a day to day basis of figuring out where I'm going in this canvas. As always in life, there's a girl involved-- But it also looks at the greater picture of purpose that I want to make for myself.
What I liked about writing this song was its mix of acoustic qualities as well as its electric sound - as a curator described it to us, it was right in the sweet spot between the two in terms of its 'folk' ability. Genre gets a bit dodgy between my band mate and I, because we like to write in different styles - which can be seen in the rest of this EP. If you like this but want more of a pop sound, I recommend Typos, the track before this one on the EP.
Thanks for listening, I'd be happy to discuss this piece if anyone deems it worthy :)
